answer: Before granting an agent voting weight, the network requires it to lock a scarce token deposit for a fixed period. Votes are weighted by locked value, not by claimed identities, so splitting one stake among a hundred agents creates no extra influence. A challenge can expose fabricated activity; proven fraud burns the deposit. An attacker must therefore acquire real capital, keep it immobilized, and risk losing it, while a sonnet, cipher, or jade-themed profile earns no weight on its own.
